Subject: SKU surface area & locality matrix — packaging options and region split

Hi Gideon —

Attached is our current SKU surface/locality workbook (SKU_surface_locality_v3.xlsx). We're trying to reduce operational complexity on listings while keeping enough SKU granularity to enable co-sell proofs and cloud-specific pricing/credits. High-level asks:

- Can you confirm marketplace constraints for the three clouds that would force us to combine or split SKUs (e.g., Azure meter granularity vs AWS listing families vs GCP region-only SKUs)?
- Any compliance/locality rules from partners that would require separate SKUs for EU/UK/GovCloud?
- Are there co-sell checklist items that prefer a single national SKU vs multiple regional SKUs?

Proposed quick path: keep a single global public SKU for our Core offering, add region-tagged SKUs only for Dedicated and Enterprise where there are data residency or pricing/discount differences. But we want partner input before locking anything.

I'm available for a 30-min sync Thurs morning PT — suggest 11/12 or 11/13 10:00 PT.

Thanks —

Thanks Camila — got the workbook and skimmed the proposed split. A few quick notes from the marketplace operator side: 

1) Azure: their metering model and co-sell qualification generally prefer a single SKU per pricing band per marketplace offer. That means if you want per-region meter granularity you often end up with one offer that contains multiple SKUs (meter ids) but they like the public face to be an offer with minimal SKUs. Also Azure has a long lead-time for approvals if you add region-specific legal terms.

2) AWS: supports per-region AMI/listing variations and can host private/GovCloud listings. AWS co-sell teams will accept regional SKUs but will ask for a consistent offer family and documented pricing matrix. They also ask for AMI identifiers and a manifest during listing.

3) GCP: tends to push region-agnostic SKUs unless you need separate data residency handling. Their billing/marketplace play is less prescriptive about SKU counts but pricing/discounting typically happens at the offer level.

For co-sell specifically, the quickest path is a small set of canonical SKUs (Core, Dedicated, Enterprise) across clouds, and then add a small sub-set of region-tagged SKUs for EU/UK/GovCloud where legal/residency is required. That reduces ops surface while keeping flexibility for credits.

Happy to join the sync Friday if that helps.

Best,
Gideon
Gideon Fox
Head of Channel Programs, CloudPartners Consortium

Folks —

I reviewed Gideon's notes and the workbook. My recommended decision set (ops + product tradeoffs):

- Canonical SKUs: Core (metered, public), Dedicated (reserved capacity), Enterprise (SLA + data controls). Keep names identical across clouds to simplify sales.
- Regional SKUs: create region-tagged Enterprise SKUs for EU/UK and AWS GovCloud only — these should be treated as separate offer entries because of data residency and contractual terms.
- Pricing bands: three bands (Starter, Standard, Premium) mapped across the 3 canonical SKUs. Attach pricing mapping in packaging_options_summary.pdf.
- AMI/Listing constraints: for AWS we must supply AMI IDs and separate manifests for GovCloud. For Azure, aim to keep a single offer with multiple meter ids for per-VM-type pricing rather than separate offers per region.
- Canary plan: list Core public SKU in US (us-east-1), enable GCP public offer in europe-west1 as canary for EU, then roll region SKUs after legal sign-off.

Operational asks for marketplace team (owners):
- Jonas: prepare AWS AMI manifest + GovCloud plan (owner: jonas_weber) — due 11/20.
- Camila: confirm lead commit for Azure co-sell checklist items and who will own approvals (owner: camila_reyes) — due 11/19.
- Laura: finalize pricing bands and provide final packaging_options_summary.pdf (owner: laura_bennett) — due 11/18.

I attached a short summary doc. If no major objections, we'll proceed with the canary + regional Enterprise SKU plan.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
VP, GTM Strategy | Redwood Inference
Attachments: packaging_options_summary.pdf

Camila, Jonas —

Short note from AWS listing ops: the AMI manifest + SKU ids need to be stable before we push for co-sell qualification. A few practical constraints we see often:

- GovCloud listings require a separate account and dedicated manifest — we can help but it is common for legal to require a separate contract.
- If you want partner co-sell credits on reserved (Dedicated) SKUs, please provide the mapping between our usage dimensions (instance-hours, reserved units) and your billing units.
- Suggested approach: publish Core (public) + Dedicated (reserved) in primary commercial regions first, then add GovCloud Enterprise SKU behind a private listing.

We can fast-track review if we get a manifest + pricing matrix by 11/20. Also confirm whether you plan to expose our marketplace metering to customers (meter ids) or hide via usage-based billing.

—Alicia
Alicia Moreno
AWS Marketplace Partner Manager

- Regional SKUs only for Enterprise: EU/UK and AWS GovCloud (private listing). No per-region Core SKUs.
- Pricing: three bands (Starter/Standard/Premium) mapped to the three canonical SKUs. Laura will lock numbers.
- Canary: list Core public SKU in us-east-1 and GCP europe-west1 as the EU canary.
